messages.text: Monday, November 2 · Canton, Michigan
Foggy morning, ancient Mars rocks, and Day of the Dead crafts
A foggy start to November will warm to a high near 81°F, with a low around 56°F. Today offers a chance to explore ancient Martian geology or engage in cultural crafts in Ann Arbor.
Expect fog today with a high near 81°F and a low around 56°F; there is a 3% chance of precipitation.
Sunrise is at 7:09 AM and sunset is at 5:26 PM, with the moon in its Last Quarter phase, 45.7% illuminated.
Ann Arbor cultural explorations

In Ann Arbor, consider the SAPAC Care Collective's JoyLab for Day of the Dead crafts at the Michigan Union starting at 5:30 PM, or a screening of "The Chinese Mayor" at the Hatcher Graduate Library at 5:30 PM.
This week, look ahead to the 862 Meeting on November 4th at 6:30 PM.
Plymouth considers residential compatibility ordinance updates

The Plymouth City Commission is undertaking an "expanded approach" to update its zoning regulations with a new Residential Compatibility Ordinance. This effort involves a thorough review of existing residential zoning before new provisions are drafted.
Upcoming celestial events and local meetings
Watch for the Southern Taurids meteor shower peaking on November 4th. Locally, the 862 Meeting is scheduled for November 4th at 6:30 PM.

Tuesday, November 3 · Canton, Michigan
Foggy mornings, ancient Mars rocks, and local tax questions
A foggy start gives way to a warm, overcast day. Local voters face decisions on museum millages, while science offers a glimpse into Mars' ancient past and a potential new dwarf planet.
Expect fog today with a high near 81°F and a low around 56°F; there is a 3% chance of precipitation.
Sunrise is at 7:10 AM, sunset at 5:25 PM, with the moon Last Quarter and 34.9% illuminated.
Local choices and ancient history
Voters in Wayne and Oakland counties can decide on millages for the Charles H. Wright Museum of African American History and the Detroit Historical Society.
Tomorrow brings two meetings: an 862 Meeting at 6:30 PM and an RPM Meeting at 7:00 PM.
Museum millages and zoning updates on local ballots

Voters in Wayne and Oakland counties will consider millages for the Charles H. Wright Museum of African American History and the Detroit Historical Society, potentially funding free admission and outreach. Plymouth's City Commission is also reviewing zoning regulations with an "expanded approach" to a new Residential Compatibility Ordinance.
Looking ahead to the Southern Taurids
Keep an eye out for the Southern Taurids meteor shower, with its peak expected on November 4th. The next new moon is November 9th.
